instruction: Change the default font of this document to 'Times New Roman'.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(2);

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully converted comma-separated text to a table in LibreOffice Writer by selecting the text, opening the Table menu, using Convert Text to Table with comma as separator.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can select text, navigate Writer menus, interact with dialogs (Convert Text to Table), set options in dialogs, click OK to apply changes
metadata.task_rationale: Tests font modification in Writer, requiring Select All + font change or modifying the Default Paragraph Style. Related formatting task that leverages demonstrated Writer navigation skills.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing the default font to Times New Roman. Getter reads the docx and extracts the Normal style font name and most common body font. Metric gives 0.5 for style default match and 0.5 for body text match, enabling partial credit.

scoring_breakdown.default_style_font: 0.5 - Normal style font set to Times New Roman
scoring_breakdown.body_text_font: 0.5 - Most common body text font is Times New Roman

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly extracts Normal style font name (default_font) and most common body text font weighted by character count, which are the two relevant signals for verifying a default font change.
Metric correctly handles expected parameter for type='rule' — directly accesses expected.get('expected_font') without incorrectly wrapping in rules/type layers.
Case-insensitive comparison is appropriate for font name matching.
Postconfig correctly saves the document (Ctrl+S) before getter reads the file, ensuring fresh state.
Partial credit scoring (0.5 style + 0.5 body text) is a reasonable design for this task.

Minor concern: if existing text has explicit font overrides in runs, most_common_font may not change even after correctly setting the default font style. However, partial credit (0.5 for style match) mitigates this gracefully.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Consider also checking the document's theme/default fonts (doc.styles['Normal'].font.name may not capture all ways LibreOffice sets a default font, e.g., via Format > Character or default template changes), though current approach covers the most common case.
